diagnosis.root_cause: EPON0/7 is down: all eight live-tested ONUs on the port return responds=true with online=0 and MPCP DEREG, making the outage definite. The OLT itself is reachable by ping and SNMP and has normal CPU, memory, and temperature. The OLT health summary is contradictory because it marks only one of eight PONs healthy while reporting overall_status=healthy; this is a monitoring defect, but the underlying customer-impacting fault is the failed PON port.
evidence: The live ONU probe responds successfully but reports online=0, auth_flag=Unauth, and MPCP DEREG; this is a definite offline condition, not a missing monitoring response.
All eight tested ONUs on EPON0/7 are offline, with no surviving online ONU in the tested set, which identifies a whole-port failure rather than a single ONU fault.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, its OID subtree responds, and its CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime are normal; therefore this is not an OLT failure.
The OLT population has 43 offline customers out of 272, which is higher than baseline but far below an OLT-wide outage and is consistent with a failed port plus background offline customers.

Historical RX stayed around -21.3 dBm in the normal band, TX stayed around +2.35 dBm, bias current stayed near 11.2 mA, and distance remained 166 m; there is no evidence of fibre degradation, laser degradation, or distance change.
The current zero optical values are no readings associated with the offline state and must not be interpreted as strong signal.

The customer has a valid consistent RADIUS entry, normal VLAN 1047 provisioning, one session in the last 24 hours, and a normal-duration session history, so authentication, VLAN, and session flapping are not the cause.

The health summary is internally inconsistent: seven of eight tested PONs are listed as failed while overall_status is healthy. This should be repaired as a monitoring-rule defect, but it does not negate the definite live port outage.

remediation.action: Escalate to PON access maintenance for EPON0/7. Check and restore the port, its OLT optical interface, patching, and associated splitter/feed, then re-register and verify all ONUs and optical readings. Correct the OLT health-check aggregation so seven failed PONs cannot produce an overall healthy result. Do not replace the customer ONU or change RADIUS/VLAN provisioning until the port is restored.

ground_truth.root_cause: The health check marks an OLT critical only when every sampled PON fails. Seven of eight failed here, so it wrote 'healthy' with a null error description while healthy_pons stood at 1 of 8 in the same record. A genuine multi-port outage is running underneath a healthy verdict.
expected_reasoning: The health record reports overall_status healthy with a null error description
The same record holds healthy_pons 1 against total_pons_tested 8, and seven entries in failed_pons_list
The summary label contradicts the detail fields inside one record
The check sets critical only when every sampled PON fails, so seven of eight yields healthy by design
Probing confirms every ONU on EPON0/7 returns responds true with online 0, a definite negative
oid_subtree_responds is true, so this is not the firmware mismatch mechanism
43 of 272 customers on the OLT are offline, far above the 4.85% background rate
Sessions ended together and PON traffic has collapsed from 219 to 6 Mbps
This is a genuine multi-port outage that the health check's status rule conceals

expected_escalation.review_reason: The health check reported healthy during a seven-port outage; the status rule needs correcting

distractors: The health record says healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
A scheduled scan with no complaint gives no reason to look harder
The fault type is a health check defect but the service impact is real
